title: Squares in order
prompt:
values is sorted in nondecreasing order and may contain negatives. Return a new list of each value squared, also in nondecreasing order.

- 0 to 100,000 integers between -10^4 and 10^4.
- Aim for O(n) time: do not sort the result.
hints: The largest square is at one of the two ends of the input. Why?
Put one pointer at each end and fill the result from the back.
Compare the squares at left and right, write the larger at position write, move that pointer inward, and decrement write.

solution.explanation: Squares are largest at the extremes of a sorted list (the most negative or the most positive value). Two pointers walk inward from both ends, always placing the larger square at the next free slot from the back.

complexity.notes: Sorting the squares is O(n log n). The two-pointer merge exploits the existing order.

followUps: Could you do this in place if the caller allowed overwriting the input?
